Role Overview

We are hiring US-based academic chemists to support the curation and evaluation of high-quality chemistry data for frontier AI models and research laboratories.

This is the Senior Reviewer track of the project. You will review complex chemistry problems and AI-generated solutions, resolve disagreements among reviewers, develop evaluation frameworks, and serve as a subject-matter advisor to client teams assessing AI model outputs.

This opportunity is designed for chemistry faculty and experienced researchers interested in applying their academic expertise to rigorous AI evaluation, scientific reasoning, and reliable AI training infrastructure.

What You’ll Do Day-to-Day

  • Conduct senior-level reviews of complex or ambiguous chemistry problems and AI-generated solutions.
  • Evaluate responses for scientific accuracy, logical consistency, mathematical correctness, clarity, and adherence to instructions.
  • Verify chemical reactions, mechanisms, structures, calculations, nomenclature, units, assumptions, and conclusions.
  • Identify factual errors, unsupported claims, unsafe recommendations, and invalid scientific reasoning.
  • Facilitate the structured resolution of disagreements among chemistry reviewers.
  • Develop and refine evaluation rubrics, review guidelines, and quality standards.
  • Provide expert advisory support to client teams reviewing AI model performance.
  • Write technically rigorous, publication-quality explanations and reviewer feedback.
  • Provide consultation within relevant chemistry specializations.
  • Document review decisions and scientific consensus clearly and consistently.
  • Follow all project protocols, confidentiality requirements, and quality standards.

Required Qualifications

  • PhD in Chemistry, Chemical Sciences, or a closely related discipline from an accredited institution.
  • Faculty appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor or above at an accredited US university or academic institution.
  • At least three years of postdoctoral, faculty, or equivalent professional research experience.
  • Active involvement in chemistry research, teaching, or academic supervision.
  • Strong command of chemical principles, quantitative reasoning, and laboratory practices.
  • Demonstrated publication record in peer-reviewed chemistry or interdisciplinary scientific journals.
  • Experience teaching undergraduate or graduate-level chemistry courses.
  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to explain complex chemical concepts clearly.
  • Ability to evaluate multiple valid approaches and determine whether conclusions are scientifically defensible.
  • Experience reviewing technical papers, research submissions, examination questions, or scientific content.
  • Ability to lead and document expert consensus.
  • Strong attention to detail and disciplined adherence to evaluation protocols.

Relevant Areas of Expertise

Expertise in one or more of the following areas is preferred:

  • Organic chemistry
  • Inorganic chemistry
  • Physical chemistry
  • Analytical chemistry
  • Biochemistry and chemical biology
  • Medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry
  • Computational and theoretical chemistry
  • Materials and polymer chemistry
  • Environmental chemistry
  • Electrochemistry
  • Surface and colloid chemistry
  • Spectroscopy and chemical characterization
  • Chemical thermodynamics and kinetics
  • Catalysis and reaction mechanisms
  • Synthetic chemistry
  • Industrial and process chemistry

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience with AI evaluation, scientific data annotation, or large language model research.
  • Experience developing scientific rubrics, benchmarks, or assessment frameworks.
  • Familiarity with computational chemistry or scientific tools such as Python, MATLAB, R, ChemDraw, Gaussian, ORCA, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with molecular modeling, simulations, spectroscopy, or scientific data analysis.
  • Prior journal peer-review or editorial experience.
  • Service on research, academic, grant-review, safety, or ethics committees.
  • Experience mentoring graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, or junior faculty.
  • Active participation in the American Chemical Society or another recognized chemistry organization.
  • Familiarity with evaluating AI-generated chemical structures, mechanisms, calculations, and scientific explanations.

Performance Expectations

  • Take senior-review responsibility for assigned case batches.
  • Deliver scientifically accurate and defensible evaluations.
  • Maintain consistent quality and reliability across assignments.
  • Clearly document errors, assumptions, calculations, mechanisms, and review decisions.
  • Collaborate constructively with other faculty-level reviewers.
  • Communicate professionally with client teams during advisory sessions.
  • Meet agreed deadlines and project quality requirements.
  • Maintain confidentiality and comply with all project protocols.

Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure

Applicants must disclose any active equity, advisory, consulting, research-funding, or paid relationships with:

  • Artificial intelligence companies
  • Chemical, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or materials companies
  • Scientific software or laboratory technology companies
  • Research organizations whose work may appear in project content
  • Other commercial entities relevant to assigned cases

Disclosed conflicts will not automatically disqualify an applicant but may be considered when assigning work.

Perks of Freelancing with Turing

Evaluation Process

  • An updated CV containing faculty appointment and research details

Shortlisted applicants will complete:

You will also mentor trainers, maintain quality standards, and drive consistent delivery of challenging technical tasks.

  • Lead and mentor a pod of technical trainers, ensuring consistent quality, productivity, and timely delivery of scientific and engineering tasks.
  • Review technical tasks end to end, including problem statements, codebases, circuit netlists, hardware description languages (HDL), datasets, computational environments, reference solutions, and automated tests.

  • Identify unreliable tests caused by nondeterministic behavior, race conditions, hardware-dependent performance thresholds, or simulation convergence issues.
  • Review automated graders to ensure they evaluate meaningful technical outputs such as functional correctness, performance, frequency response, waveforms, timing, efficiency, and system behavior.
  • Identify technical inaccuracies, flawed assumptions, incorrect tolerances, and opportunities to bypass computation, simulations, or automated evaluations.
  • Provide clear, actionable technical feedback, track revisions, and ensure quality issues are resolved before task approval.
  • Onboard trainers, allocate work, monitor quality and throughput, escalate blockers, and maintain technical documentation and best practices.

What we're looking for:

  • Ph.D., postdoctoral experience, or equivalent advanced technical experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Strong programming skills in C/C++, Rust, Python, Julia, Fortran, MATLAB/Octave, or hardware description languages (HDL), with advanced Linux and terminal proficiency.
  • Hands-on expertise in at least one major area: parallel computing, systems programming, scientific software development, circuit simulation, signal processing, power systems, or digital hardware design.
  • Strong understanding of algorithms, computational systems, numerical methods, software testing, or electrical engineering principles.
  • Experience reviewing complex codebases, technical implementations, engineering simulations, or research outputs.
  • Ability to evaluate algorithm correctness, computational performance, numerical accuracy, concurrency behavior, and reliability of technical results.
  • Strong analytical judgment with the ability to identify technical errors, edge cases, race conditions, and flawed engineering assumptions.
  • Experience mentoring, reviewing, or leading small technical teams.
  • Excellent written communication skills for providing precise technical feedback and documenting quality standards.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with HPC and systems development tools such as MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, LLVM/GCC, CMake, gdb, Valgrind, perf, sanitizers, or Slurm.
  • Familiarity with electrical engineering and hardware simulation tools such as ngspice, Xyce, Icarus Verilog, Verilator, GHDL, Yosys, pandapower, PyPSA, MATPOWER, openEMS, GNU Radio, or QEMU.

  • Experience developing technical benchmarks, programming challenges, simulation-based evaluations, or automated grading systems.
  • Experience developing or evaluating AI coding agents, terminal-based agents, or LLM-generated technical solutions.
  • Open-source development or maintainer experience, particularly reviewing and validating external contributions.
  • Industry experience in semiconductors, high-performance computing, power utilities, telecommunications, or embedded systems.
  • Prior experience in AI training, technical quality control, benchmark development, or evaluation programs.
